Subject: Draft MSA appendix — SOC2 evidence & pen-test timing

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking the call last week. Legal at Acme asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so we can move our procurement review forward. Two areas we need clarity on for the MSA security exhibit before we finalize:

1) SOC 2 evidence: Can you confirm which reports and artifact owners Redwood will share (summary report vs full SOC2 Type II), and the cadence for delivering supporting artifacts for our internal reviewers?
2) Penetration testing / penetration notice language: Our security team prefers a 30-day calendar notice and a maximum 48-hour staging access window per rolling quarter; we want to ensure you can accommodate or provide an alternate.
3) Evidence handoff mechanics: preferred channels (SFTP vs shared Drive), an evidence owners matrix, and a sample timeline for initial onboarding (first 90 days).

If you can send a short plan with owners and a proposed evidence calendar by EOD tomorrow that would unblock legal. I copied our security lead on this thread.

Best,
Jenna

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Draft MSA appendix — SOC2 evidence & pen-test timing

Jenna —

Thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below and I'll follow up with a one-page plan and calendar (and attach our SOC2 summary) within the hour:

SOC2: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II summary (Redacted report) and a controlled set of artifacts tied to the relevant Trust Services Criteria. We cannot provide raw logs or customer-segregated production backups. Our standard evidence cadence for new enterprise customers is: initial onboarding packet (T+7 business days), quarterly updates (if there's new evidence), and on-request evidence for reasonable auditor requests with a 5-business-day turnaround for standard artifacts.

Pen test: We typically require 14 days notice for scheduled full-scope tests, but we can accept a 30-day notice in the MSA if Acme needs it. For short staging access windows we can offer a guarded 48-hour slot per quarter; that will require scoped IP allowlists and a runbook for escalation. We'll propose exact guardrails in the plan.

Channels: Preferred is a secured, customers-only folder in Google Drive (audit logs and artifacts are read-only), with SFTP as an alternative for bulk deliveries. Evidence owners: I'll map engineering owners and legal contacts in the matrix.

On the plan: attaching a short SOC2 summary and the draft evidence matrix.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Team,

Looping in legal ops points I want to capture for the response to Acme so Ben's note to Jenna is defensible from a legal perspective:

- SOC2 scope: confirm we provide a redacted Type II report + mapping to assertions. We do not disclose internal control narratives beyond the redacted report.
- Pen test notice: Accept 30-day notice in contract but include a carveout for emergency or third-party mandated testing with defined escalation and a requirement that tests be non-destructive and follow our penetration testing runbook.
- Audit rights: propose a bounded inspection approach — sample-based or time-boxed inspections rather than unlimited access. Clarify that privileged inspection requiring access to production must be scheduled and staffed by Redwood for the agreed narrow windows.
- Evidence delivery: for auditor requests, attach a request template and a 5-business-day SLA response for standard artifacts; anything beyond (live DB extracts, raw logs) will require exec-level approval and separate data access agreement.

I'll draft contract language suggestions for the security exhibit and the order form addendum. Ben — give me the filenames you attached and the drive link so I can reference them in the redline suggested text.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Jenna —

Quick answers:

1) Control screenshots in the matrix are operational artifacts (evidence exports produced by our internal tooling) — they're sanitized for PII and provided as time-stamped PDF exports. We will indicate whether a particular artifact is documentation-only vs system-generated in the matrix.

2) We are open to AuditCo submitting requests directly provided: (a) Acme security sends a single intake point and authorizes AuditCo (copying your intake address), and (b) AuditCo uses our request template and respects the 5-business-day SLA for standard artifacts. Any ad-hoc asks for raw logs or production extracts will require exec approval and a separate data access agreement.

I've attached the evidence matrix and the pen-test calendar (ICS) — Laura will host the kick-off and provide the calendar invite. If the above sounds good, Karthik will propose redline language to the security exhibit and we'll aim to have a signed addendum next week.
